Subject: Private connectivity decision framework & next tests

Hi Luke —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + the next steps we discussed so your team can share with InfraOps: 

Summary (what we heard)
- FintechCo priority: strict data-plane isolation for customer data, prefer air-gapped or one-way control plane; low-latency inference for fraud scoring (P99 < 120ms target).
- Current constraint: internal procurement needs concrete network and control-plane requirements to evaluate hyperscaler options vs a private deployment.

How Redwood differentiates vs hyperscalers (summary)
- Unified API + private control plane option (customer-managed VPC) so you get consistent runtime behavior across hosted and private deployments.
- Smart routing & local caching to meet latency SLOs while minimizing egress.
- Production tooling: token-level cost breakdowns and model rollouts (helps with ops and regression monitoring).

Proposed technical next tests (what will help you decide)
1) Control-plane connectivity check (goal: confirm whether one-way control plane is acceptable): traceroute/port verification from your management network to our control-plane endpoints. Owner: InfraOps.
2) Data-plane isolation validation: small on-prem POC (single-node inference in your VPC) to validate KV cache behavior and latency under realistic load. Owner: FintechCo + Redwood SE.
3) Air-gap feasibility sketch: we can provide a runbook for a fully air-gapped on-prem package (what we can support vs what would be self-managed). Owner: Redwood Security.

Attachments: I attached a short matrix comparing Redwood vs hyperscaler options and a connectivity test plan (high-level steps you can hand to InfraOps).

Can you confirm: 1) who on InfraOps should run the traceroutes, and 2) do you have a preferred 60-minute slot next week for a technical sequencing call (we suggest Mon 6/8 or Tue 6/9, 10–11am PT)?

If helpful, I’ll loop Ben Carter (SE) into the technical call and Marissa for procurement cadence.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to a short POC so you can benchmark latency and isolation tradeoffs empirically.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Phone: +1 (415) 555-0183

Aisha —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from InfraOps after a quick look at the plan: 

1) Control-plane connectivity: we need specifics on required outbound ports and FQDNs. Hyperscalers typically allow VPC endpoints + private networking, so the cost/operational tradeoff matters. Are your control-plane endpoints static IPs or hostname-based?

2) Air-gap: our security team prefers full air-gap but might accept a one-way control plane if data never egresses. We need to understand whether Redwood supports a pull-only update channel (control plane pushes are blocked).

3) POC timing and scope: we can allocate a test VM in a staging VPC for the data-plane latency test. Our tentative timeline is to have InfraOps review the connectivity checklist by 6/10 and run traceroutes the week of 6/14.

I'll attach a quick network drawing (network-drawing-v1.png) that shows our current network zone layout. Also, budget note — procurement prefers vendor comparisons with a per-100k-token baseline; any ballpark numbers you can share given the POC profile would help.

Luke
Director, Platform Engineering
FintechCo

Thanks Luke — helpful notes. Quick answers inline, then proposed next steps: 

1) Control-plane endpoints: hostnames (control.redwood-inference.com) mapped to a small pool of regional IPs (can provide a CIDR block). We can provide a static ASN-friendly list for firewall allowlists; we do not require inbound connectivity from your network.

2) One-way control plane: we support a pull-style model for updates (your nodes poll the control plane on an outbound-only connection). For fully air-gapped customers we provide an on-prem package; that requires a slightly longer deployment window but preserves data-plane isolation.

3) POC pricing estimate: for a short benchmark (100k tokens / 24h test) estimate ballpark is ~$120 (hosted) vs ~$90 (private on-reserved capacity) — final numbers will be in a formal quote from Marissa.

Proposed next steps (we'll own coordination):
- By 6/10: Redwood provides firewall allowlist + explicit port list + CIDR. (Owner: Aisha)
- Week of 6/14: InfraOps runs traceroutes and basic connectivity checks against the provided endpoints and returns results. (Owner: FintechCo)
- 6/16–6/20: Short on-prem data-plane latency POC (single-node) with Redwood SE (Ben) to run the 100k-token workload. (Owners: FintechCo + Ben)
